coastline.source: GSHHG high-resolution polygons as published by the hosted ArcGIS FeatureServer; source lineage is the GSHHG shoreline database maintained by Wessel & Smith with NOAA involvement.
coastline.fallback_source: Local shoreline contours traced from the bundled 2048 × 1495 GSHHS-intermediate water mask; 82 contour paths and 3,661 WGS84 vertices. The live GSHHG high-resolution vector layer replaces this fallback when the service is available.
coastline.runtime_method: ArcGIS FeatureServer query for polygon features intersecting the Black Sea regional bounding box; polygons are rasterized to the local water mask and their L1 edges are rendered as a high-resolution line buffer
coastline.hierarchy: GSHHG levels L1 land/ocean, L2 lake/land, L3 island-in-lake/lake, L4 pond/island
coastline.quality_note: Live GSHHG high-resolution vectors provide the most detailed available coastline layer. The bundled contour fallback preserves the exact outline of the local GSHHS-intermediate mask at its native raster scale. Neither layer is a cadastral or hydrographic-navigation survey. The runtime feature query is optional and bounded per request; the bundled intermediate-resolution mask remains available when the network, service, or browser CORS policy prevents the high-resolution update.
coastline.release_note: The hosted FeatureServer page describes the layer as GSHHG/GSHHS high resolution; a precise package version is not asserted by this project.

relief_texture.source: ETOPO1 shaded-relief image bundled with the Basemap data package
relief_texture.note: The 4K-wide albedo export is resampled from a 255 × 135 native ETOPO1 crop and is used only as a local visual fallback for surrounding terrain; it is not a numerical elevation/bathymetry DEM. The hillshade layer is separately requested in WGS84 geographic coordinates and clipped to the live/fallback land mask before display, so its UV extent matches the geographic terrain mesh.
relief_texture.detail_albedo: black-sea-relief-albedo-detail.webp: a gentle contrast/sharpness treatment of the same source texture; no new geographic data or synthetic coastlines are added.
relief_texture.detail_normal: black-sea-terrain-detail-normal.webp: a tangent-space display normal map built from the bundled low-resolution height fallback with restrained procedural micro-material detail over land. It affects shading only and must not be read as new elevation data.

bathymetry_overlay.note: Live color map overlay draped on the water surface; requires internet and browser CORS support.

bathymetry_numeric.processing: The full GeoTIFF returned by the requested 15-arcsecond WCS grid is retained at its native response dimensions, then bilinearly sampled onto the projected terrain mesh in animation-frame batches. Isobaths are generated from that same native response grid. Source cells retain variable provenance and resolution; a 15-arcsecond request does not assert that each cell is a direct survey at that spacing.
bathymetry_numeric.quality_note: The 15-arcsecond WCS output is a browser-side resampling choice, not the native 2024 product grid. The published EMODnet DTM resolution is 1/16 × 1/16 arc minutes (about 115 × 115 m north-south), while individual cells may derive from different surveys, composite DTMs, satellite-derived bathymetry or gap-filling products. Consult source-reference and quality layers for local cell provenance. This educational map is not a navigation chart.
bathymetry_numeric.requested_grid_note: The 15-arcsecond WCS output grid is retained in full before mesh sampling. The rendered mesh remains an adaptive real-time representation, not one vertex per source raster cell.
bathymetry_numeric.source_native_resolution: EMODnet Bathymetry DTM 2024: 1/16 × 1/16 arc minutes (published gridded resolution for European seas); individual cells retain varied source lineage and quality.
bathymetry_numeric.browser_sampling_resolution: 15 arc-seconds requested for browser WCS sampling to keep the full regional raster within a practical memory and transfer budget; the browser raster is therefore resampled more coarsely than the 2024 native grid.
bathymetry_numeric.request_safety: The optional EMODnet WCS request has a 30-second timeout, a 64 MB response cap, a maximum 16 million raster pixels, dimension checks and exact regional-bounds checks. WMS color overlay is independent and has a 12-second timeout plus a 32 MB cap.

geometry.projection: WGS84 Lambert Conformal Conic, two standard parallels (40°N and 47°N), central meridian 34.5°E and latitude of origin 43.5°N. All terrain vertices, coastlines, grid lines, bathymetric contours, ports, labels, itinerary points and the inset chart use this one projection.
geometry.high_end_desktop_grid: 2049 × approximately 1435 vertices (chunk-built; exact ratio computed from WGS84 LCC projected bounds)
geometry.standard_desktop_grid: 1409 × approximately 986 vertices (chunk-built; exact ratio computed from WGS84 LCC projected bounds)
geometry.coarse_pointer_grid: 705 × approximately 493 vertices (chunk-built; exact ratio computed from WGS84 LCC projected bounds)
geometry.chart_inset: Uses the same projected geographic surface geometry and UV mapping as the full map; the route is transformed through the same WGS84 projection.
geometry.vertical_exaggeration: The numeric EMODnet elevation is clamped and multiplied by 0.00016 model units per metre for legibility. This is a visual vertical exaggeration and is not a physical scale model.
geometry.note: The map is an educational regional visualization, not a navigation chart. High visual mesh density does not create finer source data than the underlying DEM, and the local land-relief fallback remains coarser than the live coastline and bathymetry layers.
geometry.working_coastline_mask_pixels: 3072 × source-aspect height on desktop; 2048 × source-aspect height on coarse-pointer devices; high-resolution GSHHG vectors are rasterized to this working mask.
geometry.mesh_update_pipeline: Land DEM and numeric bathymetry are applied to the same WGS84/LCC vertex buffer through a serialized queue. Normals are recalculated in row batches after each complete raster update; updates yield to the browser between batches. Optional source updates are serialized after the local scene is visible; raster requests have response-size and pixel-count caps. Page visibility and back-forward-cache restoration settle any in-flight scene crossfade before resuming the renderer.
geometry.quality_note: High mesh density is used to sample the available raster surfaces smoothly; it does not increase source-data accuracy. Geographic placement is consistently projected from WGS84 coordinates. This educational map is not a navigation chart.
geometry.accuracy_note: All geographic layers use one WGS84 Lambert Conformal Conic transform over 26–43°E and 39–48°N. GSHHG coastline vectors and EMODnet bathymetry retain their distinct source qualities. The requested raster spacing and rendering mesh density are not claims of uniform survey accuracy; the offline ETOPO1-derived land fallback is visual only.

land_topography.processing: Numeric elevation is bilinearly sampled onto the projected terrain grid only for land cells; the WGS84 GSHHG coastline mask separates land from water. The image-server source resolution and data provenance vary spatially and are not asserted to be uniform.
land_topography.local_fallback: ETOPO1 shaded-relief-derived visual height proxy from the bundled 255 × 135 native regional crop; visual fallback only, not a precise numerical DEM.
land_topography.quality_note: ArcGIS WorldElevation3D Terrain3D is a multi-source elevation service with spatially varying source resolutions (documented service range from about 1000 m to 50 cm in some deployments). The requested output pixel size is a regional resampling grid, not a guarantee of source detail. The actual resolution/provenance varies by location. Optional network/CORS service; fallback remains the local low-resolution visual ETOPO1 proxy.
land_topography.requested_pixel_spacing: Approximately 15 arc-seconds per pixel over the 17° × 9° WGS84 extent (varies in ground distance with latitude).
land_topography.request_safety: The optional Terrain3D GeoTIFF fetch is bounded by a 14-second timeout, a 72 MB transfer cap, a maximum 12 million raster pixels, minimum dimensions, and geographic-bounds checks. Failed or blocked requests leave the local ETOPO1 visual fallback intact.

stability.terrain_raster_updates: Serialized queue shared between land elevation and bathymetry updates; geometry normals are recalculated in yielded row batches.
stability.optional_network_layers: Each network layer fails independently to a local layer; fetch response size and raster pixel count are capped.
stability.scene_transitions: Crossfade is completed before pagehide/visibility suspension and renderer is resized/resumed on pageshow from the back-forward cache.
stability.content_reveals: One-way IntersectionObserver reveals have per-element watchdogs, onInterrupt completion, document-hidden completion and bfcache recovery.
